messages:
mike: Heads-up — we got a support ticket: org=acme complaining about sudden throttles around 11:02. I can see spikes in 4xx. Can we triage?

jia: I saw that too. Quick check — metering pipeline shows ingestion lag ~6m for that key during the window. :thinking:

sam: enforcement logs show token-bucket denies at 11:02:15 for key:ACME-XYZ. The enforcement service is using the "approx_counts" live feed.

mike: right — my hunch is that enforcement is reading from the fast approximate feed, but the canonical billed counts are the aggregated pipeline (which lags). That mismatch can cause either false-deny or false-allow depending on freshness.

olivia: can you paste the query you used for the pipeline numbers?

jia: sure — quick run I did against warehouse:```sql
SELECT org_id, sum(token_count) as tokens, max(event_ts) as last_event
FROM usage_events
WHERE event_ts >= to_timestamp(1769796523)
  AND event_ts <= to_timestamp(1769800323)
GROUP BY org_id
ORDER BY tokens desc
LIMIT 10;
```

olivia: thanks. last_event here is ~6m before enforcement log. that explains some denies.

sam: also noticed the enforcement bucket implementation has a configurable burst window (60s) and reads a per-key counter that is updated by the aggregator with eventual consistency. during spikes we hit the live feed which didn't yet subtract recent events (race).

mike: so two separate issues: (1) stale canonical counts in the aggregator (ingestion lag/backpressure); (2) enforcement relying on an inconsistent fast path.

nate: proposed quick fix: make enforcement read from the raw ingestion topic for the last 2m as a supplement when available, and fall back to approx_counts otherwise. add a reconcile step to adjust token buckets when the canonical pipeline catches up.

jia: that would reduce false-denies. we should be careful to avoid double-subtracting when both sources overlap. need idempotent semantics.

olivia: UX idea — add a console flag per-tenant that shows "enforcement source" + "metering lag" so support can triage faster (and users can see why a deny happened).

sam: agree. also add a metric: enforcement_source_mismatch{org} and a histogram for enforcement_freshness_seconds. nate can add to prometheus.

mike: longer-term: we should run enforcement in "shadow mode" for 24h where we compute decisions from both sources and log diffs. then pick a threshold for safe switch.

nate: can take the prometheus + shadow run. plan:
- add enforcement_freshness_seconds gauge from enforcement service (ETA 2d)
- implement shadow evaluation that emits enforcement_decision_shadow_diff (ETA 3d)
- small reconcile job that backfills bucket adjustments when pipeline catches up (ETA 1w)

jia: quick triage steps for support now:
1) mark acme org as "allowlist-temporary" to avoid customer impact (support decision)
2) run manual backfill for minute window 11:00-11:06 using warehouse counts and adjust bucket tokens
3) turn on verbose logging for enforcement for that org for next 24h

mike: support already applied allowlist. can someone run the backfill?

olivia: I'll trigger the backfill script now. command:```bash
./tools/backfill_bucket --org acme --from 1769799600 --to 1769800320 --reason "support backfill due to pipeline lag"
```

recon-bot: Recon job queued: reconcile-run-1769800420 (will log audit to /mnt/recon/audit/1769800420.json)

sam: after backfill we should watch enforcement_decisions and billing_delta. set alert for >0.5% mismatch over 1h.

jia: also raised a ticket to reduce retention TTL in the ingestion queue — spikes cause long tails which increase lag.

mike: follow-ups: nate implement metrics + shadow run, sam add alert, olivia run the shadow for acme, jia coordinate ingestion tweaks, I'll own postmortem and customer comms.

nate: started a branch for enforcement_freshness metric: https://git.internal/redwood/enf/tree/feature/freshness-metric (will open PR today). :eyes:

olivia: thanks all. if we can get shadow diff <0.1% for 24h we can consider switching enforcement source to the hybrid approach.

mike: agreed. please post updates in this thread. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
